sources.title: TP 511E Safe Boating Guide: Safety Tips and Requirements for Pleasure Craft (03/2026)
sources.notes: Read through an automated fetch-and-summarise tool in four passes over the accessible PDF (characters 0 to 200 000 of about 209 000); the PDF was not opened directly. Supports: the guide says follow the regulations where it differs from them (p. 4); sound-signalling equipment: under 12 m a sound-signalling device such as a pealess whistle, compressed-air horn or electric horn if no fitted appliance, 12 m or more a fitted whistle, over 20 m also a bell (p. 27); show navigation lights after sunset, before sunrise and in low visibility (p. 28); Table 7 lights by vessel type citing Rules 23, 25 and 30 (power under 12 m: masthead, sidelights and sternlight, or all-round white and sidelights; sail under 20 m: sidelights and sternlight, optional red over green all-round masthead lights, or a combined lantern; sail under 7 m: torch or lantern if the others are not practical; human-powered: white torch or lantern ready in time, a watertight flashlight is acceptable, or the sail lights; at anchor under 50 m: all-round white, ball by day; under 7 m at anchor exempt away from channels, fairways and anchorages) (pp. 29-30); ECCC forecasts and CCG continuous VHF weather on 21B and WX1 to WX3 on the Pacific coast, strong wind warning 20 to 33 knots (p. 33); charts and publications legally required for the area, with a local-knowledge exception for small boats (p. 33); tide tables and current atlases (p. 34); Rules 9, 10 and 18 summarised (p. 37); large-vessel signals table (five short = get out of the way; one, two, three short) (p. 37); stay clear of large vessels, never cross ahead of them or pass between a tug and its tow (pp. 37-38); safe speed factors and 'slow is the only safe speed' in fog, rain, smoke and darkness (p. 38); responsibility for wake damage (p. 39); Rule 5 lookout and Rules 7 and 8 act early even with the right of way (p. 40); paddlers: bright colours and signalling devices within reach (p. 43); 10 km/h within 30 m of shore in listed provinces including BC inland waters, with exceptions (p. 44); keep paper charts in case GPS fails, marine GPS accuracy about 10 m (p. 50); Rules of the Road reference card (p. 63); buoy reference cards: lateral, bifurcation, fairway, isolated danger, daybeacons, cardinal, special, information (orange square), hazard (orange diamond), control (orange circle), keep out, diving, swimming, mooring (pp. 64-65). The guide gives no special right-of-way rule for paddle craft. Crown copyright; no reproduction permission seen. Paraphrase only.

sources.title: Small Vessel Regulations, SOR/2010-91 (Justice Laws full text): s. 1 definition of sound-signalling device; Part 2 Safety Equipment for Pleasure Craft, ss. 200, 205, 207, 209-216
sources.publisher: Department of Justice Canada (Justice Laws website)
sources.notes: Read through an automated fetch-and-summarise tool that quoted the wording in short segments (the page was not opened directly). Supports: 'sound-signalling device' means a pealess whistle or a compressed-gas or electric horn; Part 2 applies to pleasure craft operated in Canada (s. 200); Subpart 1 covers pleasure craft other than human-powered (ss. 203-208), Subpart 2 human-powered pleasure craft (ss. 209-211); s. 205 visual signals by length (not more than 6 m: a watertight flashlight or three pyrotechnic signals); s. 207 navigation equipment: not more than 9 m and over 9 m to 12 m: a sound-signalling appliance that meets the Collision Regulations or a sound-signalling device; navigation lights that meet the Collision Regulations (for the 9 m and under row, only if operated after sunset, before sunrise or in restricted visibility); a magnetic compass; over 12 m: a sound-signalling appliance that meets the Collision Regulations, navigation lights and a compass meeting the Navigation Safety Regulations, 2020; s. 211 human-powered craft: a sound-signalling appliance or device, navigation lights when operated after sunset, before sunrise or in restricted visibility, and a magnetic compass; s. 213 visual signal exceptions; s. 215 no magnetic compass needed on a craft of not more than 8 m that navigates within sight of seamarks. Not the official version; check the live text before release.

sources.title: Collision Regulations, C.R.C., c. 1416 (Justice Laws, Schedule 1): Rules 5-9, 12-18, 20, 23-25, 30, 32-35 with Canadian modifications
sources.publisher: Department of Justice Canada (Justice Laws website)
sources.notes: Read through an automated fetch-and-summarise tool in three passes (quotes in short segments plus close paraphrase); the page was not opened directly. Supports: Rule 5 lookout by sight and hearing and all available means; Rule 6(a) safe speed factors (visibility, traffic, manoeuvrability, background light at night, wind, sea, current, hazards, draught and depth); Rule 7(d)(i) steady compass bearing means risk of collision; Rule 8 early, positive, large alterations; Rule 9(a), (b), (d) narrow channels (keep to starboard; under 20 m and sailing vessels must not impede a vessel that can navigate only in the channel; do not cross if it impedes); Canadian Rule 9(k) (with a current, the power-driven vessel going with the current is stand-on in a narrow channel); Rule 12 sailing vessels; Rule 13 overtaking (more than 22.5 degrees abaft the beam, sees only the sternlight; keeps clear until past and clear); Rule 14 head-on both alter to starboard; Rule 15(a) crossing, vessel with the other on her starboard side keeps clear; Canadian Rule 15(b) a vessel crossing a river keeps clear of a power-driven vessel going up or down it; Rules 16 and 17 give-way and stand-on duties; Rule 18(a)-(c) responsibilities between vessels; Rule 20 lights from sunset to sunrise and in restricted visibility; Rule 23(a) masthead, sidelights, sternlight, second masthead light required at 50 m or more; Rule 23(d)(i) under 12 m all-round white plus sidelights; Rule 23(d)(ii) under 7 m and 7 knots option and Canadian Rule 23(e) that it does not apply to Canadian vessels; Rule 24(a) towing lights (two masthead lights in a vertical line, three if the tow is over 200 m; sidelights; sternlight; towing light above the sternlight; diamond shape by day for tows over 200 m); Rule 25(a)-(e) and Canadian 25(f) sailing vessel and vessel under oars lights, cone exemption; Rule 30(a), (b), (e) anchor lights and the under 7 m exemption; Rule 32 short blast about 1 s, prolonged 4 to 6 s; Rule 33 whistle at 12 m, under 12 m other means of efficient sound signal; Rule 34(a) and (d) manoeuvring and doubt signals; Rule 35(a), (b), (c), (j) and Canadian 35(l) restricted-visibility signals. Not the official version; check the live text before release.

sources.title: The Canadian Aids to Navigation System, 2023 Edition: special buoys, private buoys and daybeacons (pp. 4-5, 14, 18-20, 32-37, 48, 59-60)
sources.publisher: Canadian Coast Guard (Fisheries and Oceans Canada)
sources.notes: Read through an automated fetch-and-summarise tool (about the first 100 000 of 104 000 characters); the PDF was not opened directly. Supports: special buoys give information and are not mainly for navigation, their shape has no meaning, many are private and must meet the Private Buoy Regulations; lighted special buoys show yellow Fl 4s (ODAS Fl(5) 20s); keep-out and control buoys are under the Vessel Operation Restriction Regulations; cautionary (yellow, X topmark), anchorage (yellow, black anchor), control (white, orange open circle with orange bands, black figure or symbol inside), diving (white, red flag with white diagonal stripe), hazard (white, orange diamond with orange bands, words or symbols inside), information (white, orange square with orange bands, black words or symbols), keep-out (white, orange diamond containing an orange cross), swimming (white, marks the edge of a swimming area, may not be charted), ODAS (yellow, Fl(5) 20s); private buoys carry PRIV and the owner's name, address and phone number; upstream direction and starboard-hand aids kept to starboard when going upstream; numbers increase upstream, even numbers on starboard buoys, odd on port; port-hand daybeacon square green, odd numbers; starboard-hand daybeacon triangular red, even numbers. The mooring buoy colour was reported inconsistently by the tool, so it is not used. The phrase 'red right returning' is not in the document; lessons present it only as a memory aid. Crown copyright; paraphrase only.

sources.title: Vessel Operation Restriction Regulations, SOR/2008-120 (Justice Laws full text): s. 2(7)-(9) shoreline speed limit
sources.publisher: Department of Justice Canada (Justice Laws website)
sources.edition: Consolidation current to 2026-10-29, last amended 2025-08-13; accessed 2026-11-17
sources.notes: Read through an automated fetch-and-summarise tool (short quotes and paraphrase). Supports: s. 2(7) no power-driven or electrically propelled vessel faster than 10 km/h within 30 m of shore in listed waters, including the rivers and lakes in British Columbia (not BC coastal waters) and Nitinat River and Lake; s. 2(8)-(9) exceptions (towing a person on a course away from and perpendicular to shore; rivers under 100 m wide, canals and buoyed channels; waters with another speed limit). Not the official version; check the live text before release.
